title: Guardbroker: Validation & Runtime Sandbox for Autoscaling Policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a 'Guardbroker' component: a validation and runtime sandbox that evaluates autoscaling policy expressions, simulates expected scaling behavior against workload traces, and enforces safety limits at runtime. This ticket covers the policy schema extensions, a policy validation service with deterministic simulation, and a runtime enforcement hook that can 'quarantine' aggressive scale events behind soft approvals or rate-limited venting. Goal is to enable product and SRE teams to author richer scaling goals (composite metrics, percentile targets, cost caps) while preventing runaway scaling during spikes or misconfigurations.
acceptance_criteria: Policy language supports composite targets: weighted combination of latency_p95, token_throughput, and cost_per_token
Validation service can reload policies and run simulations over 7-day request traces within 15s for a typical tenant (<=10M requests)
Runtime hook enforces safety rules: max_scale_rate, burst_budget, and quarantine window; violations emit structured events to observability
UI shows simulation preview with expected scaling timeline and 95% confidence bands
Integration tests exercising misconfiguration cases (divergent targets, zero denom cost) pass in CI
technical_notes: Policy model: JSON-based DSL with named metrics and affine combinations; runtime uses precompiled bytecode for fast evaluation
Simulation: event-driven simulator that applies policy at discrete decision ticks using sampled arrival curves; supports warm KV cache and cold-start scenarios
Enforcement: two-plane approach: (1) Intent plane publishes desired instance_delta, (2) Guardbroker applies safety transforms (clamp, leaky-bucket) and emits final command
Failure modes: off-by-one policy loops prevented by idempotent policy evaluation and monotonic throttle
Performance budget: policy eval must cost <50us per decision per tenant under C++ fast-path, otherwise fallback to safe default policy
tradeoffs: Expressiveness vs. safety: richer DSL increases risk of unsafe policies; mitigated by sandboxed simulation and opt-in gradual rollout
Complex simulation vs. dev velocity: accurate emulation requires more infra; we keep simulation lightweight with configurable fidelity levels
Runtime complexity: two-plane enforcement adds code paths but gives transparent auditability and reversible quarantine
